drug_class: HIF-2α inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Belzutifan is used to treat certain kidney cancers, as well as tumors related to a genetic condition called Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease. It can help shrink or slow the growth of tumors in the kidneys, pancreas, and the lining of the brain and spine. Your doctor may prescribe it when surgery is not the best option or when the cancer has spread.
how_it_works: Inside your body, there is a protein called HIF-2α that can tell cancer cells to grow and multiply. Belzutifan works by blocking this protein, like putting a cap on it, so it cannot send those growth signals. This helps slow down or stop the cancer from growing without harming normal healthy cells as much as traditional chemotherapy would.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling very tired or weak, low red blood cell counts (anemia) which can make you feel dizzy or short of breath, headache, dizziness, and increased blood sugar levels. Some people also notice swelling in the arms or legs, nausea, and changes in lab values that your doctor will monitor.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious drop in oxygen levels in your blood, a condition called hypoxia, especially when you first start taking it or increase your dose. You should not take belzutifan if you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby — reliable birth control is very important. Tell your doctor right away if you feel unusually short of breath, lightheaded, or notice your lips or fingertips turning bluish, as these could be signs of low oxygen.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 120 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day, but skip it if it is almost time for your next dose — never double up.
